newsitem.title: USA: Calif. university regents OK hospital merger.
newsitem.headline: Calif. university regents OK hospital merger.

text.p: University of California Regents approved Friday the formation of a corporation that will complete the proposed merger of University of California San Francisco and Stanford University medical centers.
The Board of Regents approved the merger plan despite vocal opposition from representatives of hospital workers.

The private, nonprofit corporation, which will be called UCSF Stanford Health Care, will oversee the joint operations of the University of California San Francisco and Stanford medical centers effective by July 1997.
The merger will become final after the adoption of several other agreements, including those establishing compensation packages for physicians and other academic personnel.
University of California President Richard Atkinson will represent the Regents in the formation of a 17-member board of directors that will oversee the corporation.

Officials at the University of California San Francisco (UCSF) and Stanford initiated merger talks last year in response to the growth of managed health care and to the threat of reductions in state and federal support for academic health centers.

"UCSF and Stanford have concurred that a partnership of two academic medical centers is the best way to meet the challenges posed by the highly competitive managed care market and continue to provide support for the medical schools' teaching and research efforts," the Regents said in a statement.
The Regents said 95 percent of University of California San Francisco employees affected by the merger would be offered new positions by UCSF Stanford Health Care.
